P1.evidence: Application read back — 'I read your application. I have a bit of a headstart on you' — brief rapport about where he lives and what he does, frame agreement asked and given ('That all sound good?' 'Yeah, that's good'), and the scripted open question: 'walk me through it. What could we potentially help you with today, man?' The frame was three-part again: 'where you're at, where you're trying to get to, what's kind of been missing'.

P2.evidence: Age, height and weight taken; work and its sedentary nature confirmed; training week, results from it and diet all covered properly, including the useful follow-up 'did that help out with the joints at all?' which produced 'No, it helped me in building muscles, but it didn't help me with my joints.' The health question was asked but bundled and then closed off with a leading follow-up — 'But the joint pain, like you can still work out even though you have the joint pain, right?' — which is why P2c and P2d are partial rather than hit: an autoimmune disease was on the table and nothing was asked about medication, treating clinician, disease activity or flare pattern. Sleep and daytime energy were both skipped, and both are directly relevant to inflammatory arthritis.

P3.evidence: The rep did the deep work by the book and it returned almost nothing. 'Outside of just the arthritis... why else is it important for you to have the good physique and build up strength?' and 'What's the motivation behind the physique?' both ran, and 'If you're able to be healthy and look good shirtless, what would that do for you?' was asked twice, answered 'Nothing. I generally want to be healthy and look good. That's it.' The failure is what happened next: the impact question surfaced that the prospect had been married for three months, and instead of driving into marriage, family and the years ahead, the rep spent the moment on 'India is such a different culture than the United States, man' and moved to the pitch. It is the largest single missed opening in the batch. The limitations question was never asked either — the prospect volunteered 'I can't do heavy loads' and 'my working day-to-day life is kind of limited' unprompted.

P4.evidence: Past attempts were surfaced and their outcomes established — a year of push-pull-legs, yoga, and the reasoning about why weightlifting did not help the joints. The gap was named clearly by the prospect: 'I don't know how to get help with my joints getting stronger, you know?' What was not asked is why it stopped. He said twice that he quit — 'for the last four, five months, I've quit due to various reasons' and 'Because of personal reasons, I'm not currently working out' — and neither was ever probed. On a prospect whose whole case is consistency and pain, the reason he stopped four months ago was the single most useful unknown on the call.

P5.evidence: The two-year question ran properly and backfired: 'what is the next two, three, four, or five years look like for you if we don't actually figure this out?' produced a calm plan — moderate weightlifting plus yoga. Rather than working it, the rep conceded the point and closed the phase: 'But we're doing something about the joints either way, whether it's weightlifting, yoga, or, yeah, got it.' No settle question, no 'why not', no line in the sand. The cost of inaction was raised, answered away, and abandoned.

P6.evidence: Not attempted in any form. The rep went from 'is there anything else that you feel like I need to know' straight into a compressed description of the programme and then into price qualification. No belief question, no all-in question, and no yes was ever asked for before affordability was tested.

P11.evidence: No close was attempted on the coaching programme; the rep disqualified on price before presenting an offer to accept. The only transaction proposed was a Primal University link to be texted afterwards.

objection_plays.detail: The money objection existed only because the rep created it, and once created nothing was run against it. No isolation question, no should-versus-how reframe, no offer to explore making it work, and not one element of the financial picture — cash on hand, monthly surplus, cards, available credit, investments. The prospect's reaction to a rupee conversion was taken as the whole answer and the call was closed out four minutes later. Whether the price was genuinely unaffordable or simply unfamiliar is not established anywhere in this transcript.

SCRIPT GAP — THE PROSPECT IS BUYING A MEDICAL OUTCOME. His entire stated reason for the call is that he believes kettlebell training will strengthen his joints and relieve rheumatoid arthritis, and he checked that the rep understood the condition: 'I have a disease, rheumatoid arthritis. You know about this?' There is no scripted response for a prospect presenting an autoimmune disease as the thing the programme will fix — no screening step, no clearance requirement, and no language for setting expectations about what training can and cannot do for inflammatory joint disease. The rep affirmed the fit instead: 'I think it's a great fit.' This is the third call in the corpus to hit the same missing clinical gate and the most acute instance of it.

SCRIPT GAP — INTERNATIONAL PRICING AND PURCHASING POWER. There is no guidance for quoting a USD price into a very different economy. The rep improvised: he raised the issue himself on national grounds, gave a range of '4,000 USD all the way up to, like, 10,000 USD' that matches no sanctioned tier, then converted live to 'almost 400,000 rupees at kind of the bare minimum'. Handled with candour and without any framework, and it produced both a pricing deviation and an unqualified disqualification.
No think-about-it trigger; the call ended before a decision was ever on the table.
Newly married, but the spouse was never raised as a factor in the decision by either party.
No timing objection; the prospect wanted to start.
No fear or doubt about the programme was expressed.

notes: The mechanical parts of discovery were run competently in eighteen minutes, and then two things went wrong that have nothing to do with technique. First, a prospect with an active autoimmune joint disease was told the programme was a great fit without a single question about his treatment, and his belief that training would fix the disease was left standing. That is the coaching priority and it is a script problem before it is a rep problem. Second, the rep introduced the affordability objection himself on the basis of the prospect's country, before establishing any financial fact, and then disqualified on the reaction to it. On the process itself: Phase 6 never happened, Phase 5 was abandoned after one question, and the discovery of a three-month-old marriage was passed over in favour of a remark about cultural differences.
